dispositions.agreement: AGREE, independently confirmed against the artifacts.
independentConfirmation: DeficiencyV2 has 9 members; D9Deficiency has 10; the set difference is exactly the four the report names.

DomainDetailCode carries a DIFFERENT five (budget-exhausted plus those four); the overlap of the two vocabularies is budget-exhausted alone; their union is all nine and neither alone is. The report characterised this exactly.

newFindings.title: Coverage-scope disjointness is a stated producer obligation and is not decided at Run closure
newFindings.detail: identity sec.3 asserts scopes partition "without overlaps or omissions". The OMISSION half is enforced, for file@enumerated, by identity-model coverage_inventory_totality. The OVERLAP half is enforced NOWHERE in the reference model - there is no pairwise disjointness check over scope subjects. It is decidable from the retained scopes, so this is the same class of defect the contract set has corrected before (a stated law nothing derives or compares). I did NOT add the refusal: enforcing a new admission could refuse Runs that are lawful under the frozen bytes, and SHOULD-2 asked for a text reconciliation. My wording therefore states disjointness as a producer obligation and does not claim closure enforcement. Recommended as a candidate for the next pass or for the successor blind review to examine.

referenceControls.whatTheseControlsAre: SCHEMA-level: jsonschema validation of the new EvidenceRequirement presence law and vocabulary, of MutationReplayScopeV1/MutationParams admission and refusal, and of TypeDerivationV1 / ViewEntryV3 shape. HELPER-level: direct calls into the reference models (admit_evidence_requirement, sufficiency_v2, config_node_kind, typescript_config_graph_faults, typescript_config_graph_digest, discover_units, assign_membership, typescript_mode) over synthetic inputs. FULL RETAINED-RUN: the CB6-SHOULD-2 controls only - they call identity-model close_run over a built Run graph, which is the one place a whole retained closure is exercised in what I added. HOST ENFORCEMENT: NONE. Nothing here executes a provider, a compiler, a renderer, a ledger or a filesystem, and no control demonstrates that a host obeys any of it.
referenceControls.aggregationLimit: These are check rows and case rows, not a count of every admission and not a claim of exhaustive coverage. The workflows delta is inflated relative to distinct assertions because nine of the rows are one per NativeSufficiencyDeficiency member and twenty are one per generic mutation class; I list them individually so a reader can see which boundary each covers rather than reading 74 as 74 independent properties.
referenceControls.notMirroredImplementation: No control asserts that the model equals a second copy of itself. The parity controls compare a workflows-side mirror against the NATIVE authority document, and the config-node-kind controls compare model output against the PUBLISHED table the model reads - which is the point of the correction, not a tautology, because the previous model restated the rule inline and no published table existed to compare with.

limitations.evidenceClass: Everything above is design reference evidence over synthetic trusted inputs. No compiler, provider, repository, renderer, ledger or filesystem was executed. Passing controls is not product qualification and not a readiness grade.
limitations.schemaVsHelperVsRun: Distinguished explicitly in referenceControls.whatTheseControlsAre. Most of what I added is schema validation and direct helper calls; only the CB6-SHOULD-2 controls reach a full retained-Run closure; none is host enforcement.
limitations.disjointnessIsStatedNotEnforced: See CB6-NEW-3. The disjointness half of the reconciled sec.3 wording is a producer obligation and is not decided at Run closure. I deliberately did not add that refusal and the text does not claim it.
limitations.producerBoundaryScope: admit_evidence_requirement is a reference-model admission at the repair-preview boundary. Producer conformance in a real host remains an implementation obligation, as the relation registry already says for the anchor law.
limitations.stalePinsInTheProposedCopy: Expected and disclosed. Root refreshes pins after the final source and records, then runs the six final commands and freezes the successor. A stale-pin refusal in the proposed copy is neither a product failure nor a PASS.
limitations.notReviewed: I did not re-derive the blind review’s positive reconstruction, its 78 vector groups or its 355 retained objects, and I make no claim about them beyond the reservations recorded in evidenceReservationsAboutTheBlindReport.
limitations.successorStillOwed: A fresh, genuinely independent review and a fresh blind consumer pass on the accepted successor bytes remain required. This handoff is coauthor assent, not acceptance.

evidenceReservationsAboutTheBlindReport.standing: The report is substantive and its four normative findings are real - root confirmed them and I independently confirmed them above. These reservations are about the strength of its POSITIVE reconstruction claims and its headline counts, and they do not reduce any finding. The report is preserved unedited.
points: The four "complete positive Run graphs" do not validate against all the owning schemas. Its policy and waiver records use schemaVersion where the owning schemas require schemaFamily/schemaMajor, and its ruleProgramRef carries different fields.
The same CAP-1 capability manifest - one TypeScript provider with the Rust row absent - is reused for the Rust and both syntax runs, so those runs do not exercise their own provider rows.
The 83 "discriminating negative controls" are mixed: at least one is a Rust positive ownership assertion (N4) and two are hash-distinction positives. It is not 83 typed refusals.
Several controls are narrative or boolean rather than executed refusals.
The canonical decoder in its reference code does not demonstrate the lexical -0 and duplicate-key admission behaviour the report describes.
Its RC2 helper is incomplete, and its graph-closure claims are asserted rather than proven by the retained code.
evidenceReservationsAboutTheBlindReport.effectOnThisPass: None of the above was used to dismiss a finding. Where the report’s own code was limited I re-derived the fact from the frozen source instead - which is how CB6-NEW-1 and the CB6-ADV-2 disagreement were found.
